children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Brahman</s>, whose form is inconceivable and unmanifest, who is without qualities yet whose nature is the qualities,
whose embodied form is the support of the entire universe.

children.text: alpāvaśiṣṭe tu kṛte mayo nāma mahāsuraḥ
children.translated_text: When only a small remainder of the <s>Krita</s> age was left, a great <s>asura</s> named <s>Maya</s>,

children.text: rahasyaṃ paramaṃ puṇyaṃ jijñāsur jñānam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: desiring to know the supreme, holy secret, the highest knowledge,
the foremost <s>vedanga</s>, complete, the cause of the motions of the luminaries,
worshipped <s>Vivasvat</s> and performed very difficult austerity.

children.text: toṣitas tapasā tena prītas tasmai varārthine
children.translated_text: Pleased by that austerity and satisfied with him, who sought a boon,

children.text: grahāṇāṃ caritaṃ prādān mayāya savitā svayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Savitr</s> himself gave to <s>Maya</s> the account of the planets' movements.

children.text: viditas te mayā bhāvas toṣitas tapasā hy aham
children.translated_text: Your intention is known by me; indeed I have been pleased by your austerity.

children.text: dadyāṃ kālāśrayaṃ jñānaṃ grahāṇāṃ caritaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: I would give you the great knowledge, grounded in time, of the movements of the planets.

children.text: na me tejaḥsahaḥ kaścid ākhyātuṃ nāsti me kṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But no one can bear my radiance, and I have no leisure to expound it.
This person, a portion of myself, will tell it to you in full.
Having spoken thus, the god disappeared, after appointing a portion of himself.

children.text: sa pumān mayam āhedaṃ praṇataṃ prāñjalisthitam ||
children.translated_text: That man then said this to <s>Maya</s>, who was bowed down and standing with joined palms:

children.text: śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ pūrvaṃ yad uktaṃ jñānam uttamam
children.translated_text: Listen with a single mind to the highest knowledge formerly taught,

children.text: yuge yuge maharṣīṇāṃ svayam eva vivasvatā ||
children.translated_text: age after age, to the great seers by <s>Vivasvat</s> himself.

children.text: śāstram ādyaṃ tad evedaṃ yat pūrvaṃ prāha bhāskaraḥ
children.translated_text: This is that very primeval treatise which <s>Bhaskara</s> formerly proclaimed;
through the turning of the ages, only the distinction of time is different here.
Time is the destroyer of worlds; another time is that whose nature is computation.

children.text: sa dvidhā sthūlasūkṣmatvān mūrtaś cāmūrta ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Because of its gross and subtle forms, it is said to be twofold: embodied and unembodied.
The embodied is said to begin with the breath; that beginning with the <s>truti</s> is termed unembodied.

children.text: ṣaḍbhiḥ prāṇair vināḍī syāt tatṣaṣṭyā nāḍikā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: By six breaths there is one <s>vinadi</s>; by sixty of those a <s>nadika</s> is remembered.
By sixty <s>nadis</s> a sidereal day and night is proclaimed.
By thirty of those there is a month; the civil month is likewise by sunrises.

children.text: aindavas tithibhis tadvat saṃkrāntyā saura ucyate
children.translated_text: The lunar month is by <s>tithis</s> in the same way, and the solar is said to be by the sun's ingress.

children.text: māsair dvādaśabhir varṣaṃ divyaṃ tad aha ucyate ||
children.translated_text: By twelve months there is a year; that is called a day of the gods.
For gods and <s>asuras</s>, each other's day and night are reversed.

children.text: tatṣaṣṭiḥ ṣaḍguṇā divyaṃ varṣam āsuram eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Sixty times six of those make a divine year, and likewise an <s>asura</s> year.
Twelve thousand of those are declared to be a <s>caturyuga</s>,
in the count of solar years, multiplied by ten thousand with the numbers two, three, and ocean.
That <s>caturyuga</s> should be known as including the dawn and twilight portions.
This is the arrangement of the <s>Krita</s> and other ages according to the arrangement of the feet of <s>dharma</s>.
One tenth of the age, multiplied by four, three, two, and one,
respectively for the <s>Krita</s> age and the rest, has its own sixth part as each of the two twilights.
Seventy-one ages are here called a <s>manvantara</s>.
At its end, a junction equal in number to the years of the <s>Krita</s> age is taught, a flood of waters.

children.text: sasaṃdhayas te manavaḥ kalpe jñeyāś caturdaśa
children.translated_text: Those <s>Manus</s>, together with their junctions, are to be known as fourteen in a <s>kalpa</s>.
At the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>, a fifteenth junction, equal to the measure of <s>Krita</s>, is remembered.
Thus, by a thousand ages, a <s>kalpa</s>, which brings about the dissolution of beings,

children.text: kalpo brāhmam ahaḥ proktaṃ śarvarī tasya tāvatī ||
children.translated_text: is declared to be a day of <s>Brahma</s>; his night is of the same length.
His full lifespan is one hundred, counted by those days and nights.
Half of his life has passed; this remaining <s>kalpa</s> is the first.

children.text: kalpād asmāc ca manavaḥ ṣaḍ vyatītāḥ sasaṃdhayaḥ
children.translated_text: From this <s>kalpa</s>, six <s>Manus</s> have passed, together with their junctions,

children.text: vaivasvatasya ca manor yugānāṃ trighano gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and of the <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>, three cubed ages have elapsed.

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśād yugād asmād yātam etat kṛtaṃ yugam
children.translated_text: Of this twenty-eighth age, this <s>Krita</s> age has passed.

children.text: ataḥ kālaṃ prasaṃkhyāya saṃkhyām ekatra piṇḍayet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, having counted the time, one should combine the numbers into a single total.
As he creates planets, constellations, gods, <s>daityas</s>, and all moving and unmoving beings,
the divine years of the Creator that have passed are expressed by the number-compound <s>krita-adri-veda</s>, multiplied by one hundred.
Moving westward with great speed constantly among the constellations, the planets,

children.text: jīyamānās tu lambante tulyam eva svamārgagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: though being overcome, lag behind equally as they proceed on their own paths.

children.text: prāggatitvam atas teṣāṃ bhagaṇaiḥ pratyahaṃ gatiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore their daily motion is eastward through their revolutions.
It differs according to circumference, and by that they occupy the asterisms.
A swift-moving planet passes them in a short time, and a slow-moving one in a long time.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu parivartena pauṣṇānte bhagaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By their revolution, at the end of <s>Pausna</s>, one <s>bhagana</s> (complete revolution) is remembered.

children.text: vikalānāṃ kalā ṣaṣṭyā tatṣaṣṭyā bhāga ucyate
children.translated_text: Sixty <s>vikalas</s> make a <s>kala</s>; by sixty of those a degree is said to arise.

children.text: tattriṃśatā bhaved rāśir bhagaṇo dvādaśaiva te ||
children.translated_text: By thirty of those there is a zodiacal sign; exactly twelve of these make a complete revolution.
In a <s>yuga</s>, for the Sun, Mercury, and Venus, the revolutions are given by the number-compound <s>kha-catuska-rada-arnava</s>,
and for Mars, Saturn, and Jupiter in their fast motions, the revolutions are eastward-going.
For the Moon, the number-compound is <s>rasa-agni-tri-trimsat-sapta-bhudhara-margana</s>.
For Mars, it is <s>dasra-tri-asta-rasa-anka-akshi-locana</s>.
For Mercury's fast motion, it is <s>sunya-ritu-kha-adri-tri-anka-naga-indu</s>.
For Jupiter, likewise, it is <s>kha-dasra-akshi-veda-sad-vahni</s>.
For Venus's fast motion, it is <s>sat-sapta-tri-yama-asvi-kha-bhudhara</s>.
For Saturn, it is <s>bhujanga-sat-panca-rasa-veda-nisakara</s>.
For the Moon's apogee in a <s>yuga</s>, it is <s>agni-sunya-asvi-vasu-sarpa-arnava</s>.
For the node, moving to the left, it is <s>vasu-agni-yama-asvi-sikhi-dasra</s>.
For the asterisms, it is <s>asta-akshi-vasu-adri-tri-dvi-dvi-asta-sara-indu</s>.

children.text: bhodayā bhagaṇaiḥ svaiḥ svair ūnāḥ svasvodayā yuge ||
children.translated_text: Their own risings in a <s>yuga</s> are less than the days of asterism by their respective revolutions.
The lunar months are the difference between the revolutions of the Sun and the Moon.

children.text: ravimāsonitās te tu śeṣāḥ syur adhimāsakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When reduced by the solar months, the remainders are the intercalary months.
The civil days, when subtracted from the lunar days, are the omitted <s>tithis</s>.
From one sunrise of the Sun to the next is an earth civil day.
In a <s>yuga</s>, the lunar <s>tithis</s> are expressed by the number-compound <s>vasu-dvi-asta-adri-rupa-anka-sapta-adri</s>,
and the lunar days by <s>kha-asta-kha-kha-vyoma-kha-agni-kha-ritu-nisakara</s>.
And the intercalary-month <s>tithis</s> are expressed by <s>sad-vahni-tri-hutasanka-tithi</s>.
By the lost lunar days: Yama, wealth, the Aśvins, eight, space, arrow, and the Aśvins.
Four spaces, ocean, eight, pit, and five are the solar months.
When these are subtracted from the solar revolutions, the civil days become the days beginning with Wednesday.
Intercalary months, deficient nights, asterismal, lunar, and civil days,
when multiplied by one thousand, become in a kalpa the revolutions and the rest.
In a kalpa the forward motion of the sun's manda-apogee is seven, eight, and fires;
of Mars, the Vedas, space, and Yama; of Mercury, eight, seasons, and fires.
For Jupiter they are space, space, and apertures; for Venus, wealth, qualities, and arrows;
for Saturn's manda-apogee, cows and fires. Now for the nodes, in reverse order:
for Mars, Manus and Aśvins; for Mercury, eight, eight, and oceans;

children.text: kṛtādricandrā jaivasya trikhāṅkāś ca tathā bhṛgoḥ ||
children.translated_text: for Jupiter, kṛta, mountains, and moon; and likewise for Venus, three, space, and marks.
The revolutions of Saturn's node in a kalpa are Yama, tastes, and seasons.
The revolutions of the moon's apogee and node have already been stated here before.

children.text: ṣaṇmanūnāṃ tu saṃpīḍya kālaṃ tatsaṃdhibhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Having compressed the time of six Manus together with their junction periods,
and also with the junction at the beginning of the kalpa, and likewise of the Vaivasvata Manu,

children.text: yugānām trighanaṃ yātaṃ tathā kṛtayugaṃ tv idam
children.translated_text: the cube of three yugas has elapsed, and also this Kṛta age.

children.text: projjhya sṛṣṭes tataḥ kālaṃ pūrvoktaṃ divyasaṃkhyayā ||
children.translated_text: After removing from creation the time previously stated in divine reckoning,
these, known by the number of solar years, had elapsed at the end of the Kṛta age:
spaces-four, Yama, mountain, fire, arrow, aperture, and moon.
From that point onward these are added to the number of elapsed years of the past time.
Having been converted into months, they are combined with the elapsed months beginning with Madhu and Śukla.
These, kept separately and multiplied by the intercalary months, are divided by the solar months.
Joined with the obtained intercalary months, converted into days, and combined with the days,
they are put in two places, multiplied by the lost lunar days, and divided by the lunar days.
With the obtained deficient nights subtracted, the civil day-count at midnight at Laṅkā is obtained.
From the sun, then, come day, month, year, and the civil day-count.
Reduced by seven, the remainder gives the lord of the weekday beginning with the sun.
The number obtained from months, years, and days, multiplied by two or three and increased by one,
when divided by seven, leaves remainders to be known as the month and the year.
The mass of days, multiplied by a planet's own revolutions and divided by terrestrial days,
gives the planet, beginning with revolutions, according to its mean motion.
In the same way, one's own śīghra and manda apogees that have been said to move forward,
and the nodes, which move in reverse, are similarly subtracted from the circle.
The elapsed revolutions of Jupiter, multiplied by twelve and joined with the current signs,

children.text: rāśibhiḥ sahitāḥ śuddhāḥ ṣaṣṭyā syur vijayādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when purified and divided by sixty, become the cycles beginning with Vijaya.
This has been stated at length; in practical use, however, in brief,
the calculation of the mean positions of the planets is to be made from the desired yuga.
At the end of this Kṛta age all planets in mean motion,

children.text: vinā tu pātamandoccān meṣādau tulyatām itāḥ ||
children.translated_text: excepting the nodes and manda-apogees, reached equality at the beginning of Aries.
The moon's apogee was at the beginning of Capricorn, and its node began from Libra.

children.text: niraṃśatvam gatāś cānye noktās te mandacāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The others, being slow-moving, had reached zero degrees and are not stated.

children.text: yojanāni śatāny aṣṭau bhūkarṇo dviguṇāni tu
children.translated_text: The diameter of the earth is eight hundred yojanas, doubled;
from ten times its square the square root is the circumference of the earth.
The true local circumference of the earth is the circumference multiplied by the lambajya and divided by the radius-sine.
By that, the planet's motion multiplied by the difference in longitude is divided.

children.text: kalādi tat phalaṃ prācyāṃ grahebhyaḥ pariśodhayet
children.translated_text: The resulting kalās and so forth should be subtracted from the planets in the east,

children.text: rekhā pratīcī saṃsthāne prakṣipet syuḥ svadeśajā ||
children.translated_text: and added when the line is situated in the west; thus they become local to one's own place.
The central meridian passes between the abode of the Rākṣasas and Devaukas mountain,

children.text: rohītakam avantī ca yathā saṃnihitaṃ saraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also through Rohītaka, Avantī, and the lake that lies near them.
If the opening of the moon occurs after the time arrived at by that calculation,

children.text: yadā bhavet tadā prācyāṃ svasthānaṃ madhyato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: then, in the east, one's own place is to the east of the central line.

children.text: aprāpya ca bhavet paścād evaṃ vāpi nimīlanāt
children.translated_text: If it occurs before, it is to the west; the same applies also from the closing.
By the nāḍīs of difference between those two, one should multiply the true circumference of the earth.

children.text: ṣaṣṭyā vibhajya labdhais tu yojanaiḥ prāg athāparaiḥ
children.translated_text: Dividing by sixty, by the yojanas obtained, eastward or westward,

children.text: svadeśaḥ paridhau jñeyaḥ kuryād deśāntaraṃ hi taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: one's own place on the circumference is to be known; by them one should determine the longitude difference.
In an eastern place, the commencement of the weekday occurs when more than midnight has passed;
by the nāḍīs of longitude difference it should be specified as less in the west.
The motion multiplied by the desired nāḍīs and divided by sixty gives kalās and the rest.

children.text: gate śodhyaṃ yutaṃ gamye kṛtvā tātkāliko bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When the planet has passed, this is to be subtracted; when it is approaching, it is to be added, making it instantaneous.
One eightieth part of the minutes of the zodiac is the maximum north-south deviation.
The cool-rayed moon is deflected by its own node from the end of its own declination.
Jupiter is deflected by twice one-ninth of that; Mars by three times it.
Mercury, Venus, and Saturn's son, by their nodes, are deflected fourfold.
Thus, three, cube, aperture, sun, taste, sun, and sun, multiplied by ten,
are stated in order as the mean latitudinal deviations in minutes for the moon and the others.
Invisible forms of time, resting on revolutions,
called śīghra, manda-apogee, and node, are the causes of the motions of the planets.
Bound by their wind-ropes, by those left and right hands,
they are drawn eastward and westward, each facing its own direction according to nearness.

children.text: pravahākhyo marut tāṃs tu svoccābhimukham īrayet
children.translated_text: The wind called Pravaha impels them toward their own apogees.
Pulled east and west, they proceed with motions of different kinds.
The one standing half a revolution east of the planet draws the planet eastward;
called the apogee, when standing in the western half it likewise draws the planet westward.

children.text: svoccāpakṛṣṭā bhagaṇaiḥ prāṅmukhaṃ yānti yad grahāḥ
children.translated_text: When planets, drawn away from their own apogees by revolutions, move eastward,

children.text: tat teṣu dhanam ity uktam ṛṇaṃ paścānmukheṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: that is called positive correction in those; and negative correction in those facing west.
In the same way to the south and north also, the node, <s>Rāhu</s>, by its own speed,
casts this latitude of the moon and the others away from their declination.
The node, when it is in the western half, casts the planet's latitude northward;
when it stands in the eastern half of the revolution, it draws it away toward the southern direction.

children.text: budhabhārgavayoḥ śīghrāt tadvat pāto yadā sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: When, for Mercury and Venus, the node is similarly situated from the <s>śīghra</s> point,
then, because of that attraction by the <s>śīghra</s> point, those two are deflected in the manner stated.
Because of the greatness of its orb, the sun is drawn aside only slightly;
because of the smallness of its orb, the moon is therefore drawn aside greatly.
Mars and the others, because their bodies are small, by the deities called <s>śīghra</s> and <s>manda</s> apogees,
are drawn very far away, being extremely swift.

children.text: ato dhanarṇaṃ sumahat teṣāṃ gativaśād bhavet
children.translated_text: Therefore a very great positive or negative correction arises for them according to their motion.

children.text: ākṛṣyamāṇās tair evaṃ vyomni yānty anilāhatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Being drawn by them in this way, they move in the sky as if struck by wind.
Retrograde, very retrograde, irregular, slow, slower, even,

children.text: tathā śīghratarā śīghrā grahāṇām aṣṭadhā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also swifter and swift: the motion of the planets is of eight kinds.
Among these, very swift, the motion called swift, slow, slower, even,

children.text: ṛjvīti pañcadhā jñeyā yā vakrā sātivakragā ||
children.translated_text: and straight are to be known as fivefold; the retrograde motion is the one that also becomes very retrograde.
Now, according to those respective motions, the planets always
come to equality with observation; I shall carefully state that correction to true position.
One eighth part of the minutes of a sign is first called a half-sine.
Mixed with the quotient, lessened by division by that respectively, that becomes the second.
In this way, successively dividing the accumulated quantities by the first, and adding or subtracting the quotients,
there arise the segments, the twenty-four half-sine aggregates, in order as follows.
Principles, Aśvins, digits, oceans, makers; form, earth, mountains, seasons;
sky, digits, eight; five, zero, lords; arrows, form, qualities, moons;
zero, eyes, five, one; apertures, form, sages, moons;
space, moon, Atidhṛtis; qualities, apertures, sky, Aśvins;
sages, six, Yama, eyes; moon, fire, makers, Aśvins;
five, eight, objects, eyes; elephants, Aśvins, mountains, Aśvins;
aperture, five, eight, Yamas; Vasus, mountains, digits, Yamas; and
makers, eight, zero, fires; mountains, mountains, moon, fires;
six, five, eyes, qualities; moon, eyes, fires, fires;
Yama, mountains, fires, fires; apertures, zero, oceans, fires;
form, fire, oceans, qualities; Vasus, fire, makers, fires: these are the reverse half-sine aggregates,
when subtracted in reverse order from the radius.
Sages, apertures, pairs of Yamas; tastes, sixes, lordly sages;
two, eight, one; form, six, Aśvins; oceans, meanings, fires;
sky, seasons, Vedas; nine, mountains, meanings; directions, elephants; three, meanings, elephants;
mountains, sky, space, moon; form, earth, mountain, Śaṃkaras;
arrows, oceans, fire, one; serpents, eyes, arrows, moons;
nine, form, earth-mountain, one; elephant, one, digits, moons;
qualities, Aśvins, form, eyes; fire, fire, qualities, Aśvins;
Vasus, oceans, meanings, Yamas; horses, seasons, mountains, Aśvins;
nine, eight, nine, eyes; fire, one, Yama, fires;
elephants, fire, oceans, qualities: these are the reverse half-sine aggregates.
But the sine of maximum declination is seven, apertures, qualities, moons.

children.text: tadguṇā jyā trijīvāptā taccāpaṃ krāntir ucyate ||
children.translated_text: A sine multiplied by that and divided by the radius-sine gives an arc; this is called declination.

children.text: grahaṃ saṃśodhya mandoccāt tathā śīghrād viśodhya ca
children.translated_text: After subtracting the planet from the <s>manda</s> apogee, and likewise after subtracting it from the <s>śīghra</s> point,

children.text: śeṣaṃ kendrapadaṃ tasmād bhujajyā koṭir eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the remainder is the quadrant of the anomaly; from that come the sine of the base and also the perpendicular.

children.text: gatād bhujajyā viṣame gamyāt koṭiḥ pade bhavet
children.translated_text: In an odd quadrant, the sine of the base is from the elapsed part and the perpendicular from the part to be traversed.

children.text: yugme tu gamyād bāhujyā koṭijyā tu gatād bhavet ||
children.translated_text: But in an even quadrant, the base-sine is from the part to be traversed, and the perpendicular-sine from the elapsed part.

children.text: liptās tattvayamair bhaktā labdhaṃ jyāpiṇḍikaṃ gatām
children.translated_text: The minutes, divided by the principles and Yamas, give the elapsed sine-aggregate obtained.
One should multiply by the difference between the elapsed and the remaining and divide by the principles and eyes.
The result obtained from that is to be added to the sine-aggregate called elapsed.

children.text: syāt kramajyāvidhir ayam utkramajyāsv api smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the rule for the direct sine; it is also remembered for the reverse sines.
Having subtracted the sine, multiply the remainder by the principles and Aśvins, and divide it by their difference.
When it is added to the product of the number by the principles and Aśvins, it is called the arc.
The degrees of the sun's <s>manda</s> circumference are Manus; those of the cool-rayed moon are teeth.
At the end of an even quadrant; but at the end of an odd quadrant, both are less by twenty minutes.
At the end of an even quadrant, for the others, are meanings, mountains; sky, fires, gods; suns, nine, oceans;

children.text: oje dvyagā vasuyamā radā rudrā gajābdayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the odd end, two, mountains; Vasus, Yamas; teeth, Rudras; elephants, clouds.
Next, for Mars and the others, in the <s>śīghra</s> correction at the end of an even quadrant: meanings, fires, Aśvins;
qualities, fires, moon; sky, mountains; two, tastes, eyes; cows, fires.
At the odd end: two, three, Yamas; two, Viśvedevas; Yamas, mountains;
sky, seasons, Aśvins; space, Vedas: these are declared for the <s>śīghra</s> operation.
The difference between the odd and even ends, multiplied by the base-sine and divided by the radius-sine,

children.text: yugme vṛtte dhanarṇaṃ syād ojād ūnādhike sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: in an even quadrant becomes positive or negative; from the odd value, when less or greater, the result is true.
When the base-sine and perpendicular-sine have been multiplied by that and divided by the degrees of a revolution,
the arc of that base-sine result is the <s>manda</s> correction, a result in minutes and so forth.

children.text: śaighryaṃ koṭiphalaṃ kendre makarādau dhanaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: The <s>śīghra</s> correction is the perpendicular result; when the anomaly begins with Capricorn it is remembered as positive.

children.text: saṃśodhyaṃ tu trijīvāyāṃ karkyādau koṭijaṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: But when it begins with Cancer, the perpendicular result is to be subtracted from the radius-sine.
From the sum of the squares of that base result and perpendicular result, the square root is the hypotenuse called variable.
The base result multiplied by the radius-sine is divided by the variable hypotenuse.

children.text: labdhasya cāpaṃ liptādiphalaṃ śaighryam idaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: The arc of the quotient is the result in minutes and so forth; this is remembered as the <s>śīghra</s> correction.

children.text: etad ādye kujādīnāṃ caturthe caiva karmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: This is the operation for Mars and the others in the first and also in the fourth cases.
Now the single manda operation for the sun and moon is stated, and for Mars and the other planets,

children.text: śaighryaṃ māndaṃ punar māndaṃ śaighryaṃ catvāry anukramāt ||
children.translated_text: the śīghra, the manda, again the manda, and the śīghra operations, four in sequence.
At the mean planet one applies half of the śīghra correction, and likewise half of the manda correction;

children.text: madhyagrahe mandaphalaṃ sakalaṃ śaighryam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: at the mean planet one applies the entire manda correction and the śīghra correction as well.

children.text: ajādikendre sarveṣāṃ śaighrye mānde ca karmaṇi
children.translated_text: When the anomaly begins with Aries, in both the śīghra and manda operations for all planets,

children.text: dhanaṃ grahāṇāṃ liptādi tulādāvṛṇam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the correction of the planets is positive in minutes and so on; when it begins with Libra, it is negative.
The planet's motion, multiplied by the result from the sun's arm, is divided
by the minutes of the zodiac; the minutes are to be applied to the planet as in the case of the sun.
The mean motion of the lord of night, corrected by subtracting its own manda motion,
after making the difference of the sine of the arc and the rest, becomes negative or positive in the motion.
In the manda operation, the result from the planet's motion is to be made as for the planet itself;
the motion multiplied by the difference of the sine of the arc is then divided by the number tattva-netra.
Multiplied by its own manda circumference and divided by the degrees of the revolution, the result is minutes;

children.text: karkyādau tu dhanaṃ tatra makarādāv ṛṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: there it is regarded as positive when beginning with Cancer, but negative when beginning with Capricorn.
Having removed the manda-corrected motion from the motion of the śīghrocca,
one should then multiply that remainder by the difference between the radius and the final hypotenuse.
Divided by the movable hypotenuse, it is positive in the motion when the hypotenuse is greater than the radius;

children.text: ṛṇam ūne 'dhike projjhya śeṣaṃ vakragatir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: negative when it is less. When the greater is subtracted, the remainder becomes the retrograde motion.
When a planet is far from its own śīghrocca, with weakened rays,
its body is drawn to the left and to the right; then its motion becomes retrograde.
With the central degrees in the fourth signs, namely four, six, moon; Veda, Indra; zero, three, one; quality, eight;
and arrow, Rudra, Mars and the other planets become retrograde.

children.text: bhavanti vakriṇas tais tu svaiḥ svaiś cakrād viśodhitaiḥ
children.translated_text: By those same degrees, subtracted severally from the circle,
they abandon retrogression at their own anomalies equal to the remaining degrees.
Because of the magnitude of the śīghra circumference, Venus and Mars are in the seventh sign,
Jupiter and Mercury in the eighth, and Saturn in the ninth.
For Mars, the sun, Jupiter, and the nodes, the result born of the śīghra correction is as for a planet;
for Mercury and Venus the result is reversed, and the manda result is a third part.
From the planet diminished by its own node, or, for Venus and Mercury, from the śīghra point, the sine,
multiplied by the latitude and divided by the final hypotenuse, gives the latitude; for the moon it is divided by the radius.
When latitude and declination have the same direction, the declination is joined with the latitude;
when their directions differ, it is subtracted. The true declination is obtained as in the case of the sun.
The motion multiplied by the rising prāṇas of the planet and divided by one hundred and eighty,
joined with the obtained zodiacal prāṇas, is known as the prāṇas of its own day and night.
Having made the direct and inverse sines of the declination there, by the inverse sine
the radius diminished gives half the diameter of the day-circle, to the south or north.
The sine of declination, multiplied by the equinoctial shadow and divided by twelve,
then multiplied by the radius and divided by the hypotenuse of half the day and night, gives the caraja prāṇas.
Its arc is positive at northern declination and negative when situated separately;
in the quarter of its own day and night, the halves of day and night are known.
At southern declination the two are reversed, and the day and night are doubled.
For the lunar mansions too, by the declination increased or decreased by latitude, each in its own case,
the course of a mansion is eight hundred minutes, and likewise zero, horsemen, and mountains for a tithi.
The planet's minutes, divided by the mansion course, give the mansions; by the motion, days and so forth are obtained.
From the minutes of the sum of the sun and moon, yogas are obtained, divided by the mansion course;
the elapsed and remaining portions, multiplied by sixty and divided by the sum of the motions, give nāḍikās.
From the minutes of the moon diminished by the sun, tithis are obtained, divided by the course;

children.text: gatā gamyāś ca ṣaṣṭighnyo nāḍyo bhuktyantaroddhṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the elapsed and remaining portions, multiplied by sixty, give nāḍīs when divided by the difference of motions.

children.text: dhruvāṇi śakunir nāgaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu catuṣpadam
children.translated_text: The fixed karaṇas are Śakuni, Nāga, the third Catuṣpada,
and Kiṃstughna, from the latter half of the dark fourteenth tithi.
Thereafter the seven karaṇas beginning with Bava are called movable karaṇas;
in a month each of the karaṇas occurs eight times.
One should assign to all the karaṇas the course of half a tithi.
This true motion of the celestial wanderers beginning with the sun has been stated.
